briefing.headline: Midterms, UK‑EU food deal and Welsh budget dominate politics
briefing.overview: US voters head to the polls while the Supreme Court rules on ballot disputes. In the UK, Labour cuts ties with the Greens and Wales approves a new budget, alongside a UK‑EU food‑export agreement.

stories.title: US midterm elections
stories.what_happened: The November 3 midterm elections decide whether Republicans keep control of Congress or Democrats win a majority in one or both chambers. Live updates and analysis were provided by several outlets.
stories.why_it_matters: The outcome will shape the balance of power between the executive and legislature, a core A‑level theme in the study of the US Constitution and Congress. It also tests voter attitudes to current policy issues.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Republicans claim the vote shows public endorsement of the administration’s economic agenda.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Democrats warn the results could stall legislation on climate and health reforms.

perspectives.label: From the right
perspectives.text: Conservatives stress the importance of limited government and fiscal restraint.

key_term.definition: Elections held halfway through a president’s term to elect members of Congress.

stories.exam_use: Use as evidence of how electoral outcomes affect executive‑legislative relations in a comparative essay on US politics.

stories.title: Supreme Court rejects ballot‑setting request
stories.what_happened: The Supreme Court quickly rejected the Trump administration’s bid to force California to set aside 20,000 ballots it said were likely cast by non‑citizens. The case concerned the validity of those votes in the midterms.
stories.why_it_matters: The decision illustrates judicial review of executive actions, a key concept in the US Constitution unit. It also highlights the Court’s role in election disputes.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: The Court defended the integrity of the electoral process by refusing political interference.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Opponents say the ruling ignored concerns about voter suppression among minorities.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: Progressives view the case as part of a broader effort to restrict voting rights.

key_term.definition: The power of courts to assess the legality of actions by the executive or legislature.

stories.exam_use: Cite as an example of the Supreme Court influencing election outcomes in a short‑answer question on US courts.

stories.title: Labour ends power‑sharing with Greens
stories.what_happened: Labour’s National Executive Committee announced it will cut ties with Green councillors in 11 local authorities over a dispute about Zionism policy. The move ends existing power‑sharing arrangements.
stories.why_it_matters: The episode shows intra‑party conflict and coalition dynamics, relevant to the AQA topics of political parties and democracy. It also raises questions about party discipline versus local autonomy.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Labour says the decision protects its core values and prevents factionalism.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Green supporters claim the move undermines progressive cooperation on climate policy.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: Left‑leaning commentators warn the split could fragment the broader left vote.

key_term.definition: An arrangement where parties share decision‑making authority in a governing body.

stories.exam_use: Use to illustrate party‑level strategies and coalition challenges in an essay on UK party politics.

stories.title: Welsh Government budget approved
stories.what_happened: The Senedd passed a supplementary budget that adds £60 million for schools, childcare and the NHS after Labour backed a deal with the Welsh Government. The funding aims to address service pressures.
stories.why_it_matters: The story demonstrates how devolved administrations raise and allocate funds, linking to the AQA unit on devolution and the fiscal powers of the Welsh Government.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Welsh Labour says the extra money will improve public services and reduce inequalities.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Opposition parties argue the spending lacks a clear funding source and could increase debt.

perspectives.label: From the right
perspectives.text: Conservative voices caution against expanding the size of the public sector.

key_term.definition: The transfer of powers from the central UK government to regional bodies such as the Welsh Senedd.

stories.exam_use: Reference in a data‑response question on how devolved governments fund public services.

stories.title: UK‑EU food‑export deal announced
stories.what_happened: The UK and the EU reached a draft agreement to remove Brexit‑related red tape on food exports, a key part of the broader post‑Brexit reset. The deal will be discussed at a summit later in the month.
stories.why_it_matters: The agreement illustrates the executive’s role in foreign policy and treaty negotiation, linking to the AQA Constitution and EU relations topics. It also shows how trade issues affect domestic politics.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Pro‑Brexit officials say the deal eases trade for farmers without compromising sovereignty.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Opposition parties warn the agreement may undermine UK standards and give the EU too much leverage.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: Progressive groups stress the need for environmental safeguards in any trade deal.

key_term.definition: A negotiated arrangement between two or more states governing the exchange of goods and services.

stories.exam_use: Use as evidence of executive power in foreign affairs for a source‑based question on the UK Constitution.

compare.uk: In the UK, devolved bodies like the Senedd are debating voting rules for foreign nationals, showing how electoral law varies across the union.
compare.us: US midterm elections determine control of Congress, directly affecting national policy and the balance of power.
compare.insight: The contrast highlights how the UK’s multi‑level system allows regional electoral reforms, whereas the US uses nationwide elections to shift legislative power.

ideas_lens.text: The US poll showing voters prioritise the economy and democracy reflects liberalism’s emphasis on individual welfare and democratic participation, ideas championed by thinkers such as John Locke.

exam_question.question: Assess the extent to which recent electoral events in the US and the UK illustrate the relationship between voters and the executive.
exam_question.tip: Structure your answer by comparing the US midterms (legislative control) with the Welsh budget vote (devolved executive decisions) and use specific examples from the news.
